name: Jeremiah
description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Zedekiah is twenty one years old when he begins to reign and reigns eleven years, and he does evil in the sight of the Lord his God and humbles not himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from the mouth of the Lord.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: This fulfills the word of the Lord by the mouth of Jeremiah, that the land would enjoy her sabbaths and lie desolate to fulfill threescore and ten years.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the Lord by Jeremiah might be accomplished, the Most High stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout all his kingdom.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: In the first year of Cyrus the word of the Most High spoken by Jeremiah is fulfilled. The Lord stirs up the spirit of Cyrus to make a proclamation throughout his kingdom.

note.label: Ezra 1: Cyrus Stirred Up to Send Israel Home

points: Jeremiah is shown a rod of an almond tree, and the Most High says He will hasten His word to perform it.

note.label: Jeremiah 1: The Prophet Ordained unto the Nations

points: That's how you know it's not all about loves and kisses as far as prophecy. We're supposed to prophesy destruction. We're supposed to prophesy these things so our people may wake up, because that's what's going to happen. Destruction is headed to America. Destruction is coming to Babylon the Great. So we're going to prophesy about them. Same thing Jeremiah did.

All my familiars watch for my halting: notice that it says they waited. They waited for him. That means they were watching Jeremiah and all of his actions, waiting for him to fall, waiting for him to make a mistake, so they could be like, ah, gotcha. Oh, you remember did this, you remember did that? They got caught doing this; let's plaster it all over social media to try to defame the whole organization. Same thing that was going on during Jeremiah's time is happening today.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Pashur the priest, chief governor in the house of the Most High, hears Jeremiah prophesy, smites him, and puts him in the stocks in the high gate of Benjamin.

note.label: Jeremiah 20: The Prophet's Fire Shut Up in His Bones

points: The word came to Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, recounting that for twenty-three years, from the thirteenth year of Josiah, the Most High had risen early and spoken but the people would not hearken.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: When Jeremiah finished speaking all that the Most High commanded, the priests, the prophets, and all the people took him and said, Thou shalt surely die.

note.label: Jeremiah 26: Jeremiah Threatened for Prophesying

points: Jeremiah answers the princes and all the people that the Most High sent him to prophesy against this house and city, and tells them to amend their ways and obey, that the Most High might repent of the evil pronounced against them.

note.label: Jeremiah 26: Jeremiah Threatened for Prophesying

points: The elders also recall Urijah the son of Shemaiah, who prophesied against the city like Jeremiah; when Jehoiakim sought to kill him he fled to Egypt, but the king sent men who fetched him back and slew him with the sword.

note.label: Jeremiah 26: Jeremiah Threatened for Prophesying

points: One king knew the word came from the Most High and spared the prophet, while another king put his prophet to death; nevertheless the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah so he was not given to the people to be killed.

note.label: Jeremiah 26: Jeremiah Threatened for Prophesying

points: Jeremiah answered Amen, the Lord do so, the Lord perform thy words to bring again the vessels and the captives; but he told Hananiah not to hold on to that.

note.label: Jeremiah 28: Hananiah the False Prophet

points: Hananiah took the yoke from off Jeremiah's neck, the yoke he wore in his captivity, and broke it before all the people.

note.label: Jeremiah 28: Hananiah the False Prophet

points: He said thus saith the Lord, even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all nations within two full years; and Jeremiah went his way.

note.label: Jeremiah 28: Hananiah the False Prophet

points: Jeremiah told Hananiah the Lord had not sent him, but he made the people trust in a lie and was leading his people astray.

note.label: Jeremiah 28: Hananiah the False Prophet

points: Jeremiah sent a letter from Jerusalem to the residue of the elders, the priests, the prophets, and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried captive to Babylon, after Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, the princes, the carpenters, and the smiths had departed.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

points: Zephaniah read the letter in the ears of Jeremiah, and the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, for the Lord was dealing with Jeremiah, that was the difference.

note.label: Jeremiah 29: The Letter to the Captives

points: This was the word of the Most High that came through Jeremiah to the king, that though they fight against the Chaldeans they should not prosper.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

points: The word came to Jeremiah in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, when the king of Babylon's army besieged Jerusalem and Jeremiah was shut up in the court of the prison.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

points: The word came to Jeremiah a second time while still shut up in the prison: the Most High who made and formed the earth to establish it invites him to call, promising to answer and show him great and mighty things he knows not.

note.label: Jeremiah 33: The Branch of Righteousness and the Covenant of Day and Night

points: The word came when Nebuchadnezzar and all his army fought against Jerusalem: Jeremiah is to tell Zedekiah that the Most High will give the city into Babylon's hand to be burned with fire, and Zedekiah shall not escape.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

points: Jeremiah calls Baruch the son of Neriah, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the Most High upon the roll.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Baruch reads the words of Jeremiah in the temple in the chamber of Gemariah, in the ears of all the people.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: The princes tell Baruch to go hide himself and Jeremiah, and to let no man know where they are.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Jeremiah gives a second roll to Baruch, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the burned book, and many like words are added besides.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Zedekiah sends men to ask Jeremiah to pray to the Most High for them, while Jeremiah is still going in and out among the people, not yet put into prison.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: When the Chaldean army breaks up from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army, Jeremiah goes forth toward the land of Benjamin to separate himself among the people.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: At the gate of Benjamin a captain of the ward named Irijah seizes him, charging that he is falling away to the Chaldeans; Jeremiah answers that it is false, but Irijah will not hear him.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: Thou fallest away to the Chaldeans. Then said Jeremiah, it is false. False accusation. But he hearkened not to him. Wherefore the princes were wroth with Jeremiah, and smote him, and put him in prison. All because of a false accusation.

note.label: The Inevitability of Obsolescence & Agony of Defeat

points: Irijah brings Jeremiah to the princes, who are wroth with him, smite him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: After Jeremiah has remained many days in the dungeon and its cells, Zedekiah secretly sends for him and asks if there is any word from the Most High; Jeremiah answers there is, that the king shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: Jeremiah asks what he has offended against the king, his servants, or the people that they have put him in prison, and where now are the prophets who prophesied that the king of Babylon would not come.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: They cast Jeremiah into the dungeon of Malchiah in the court of the prison, letting him down with cords into a place with no water but mire, and Jeremiah sinks in the mire.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Abedmelech the Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs in the king's house, hears that Jeremiah has been put in the dungeon while the king sits in the gate of Benjamin.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: One of our forefathers was thrown in a pit: they cast Jeremiah into the dungeon of Malchiah and let him down with cords, and in the dungeon there was no water, but mire; that is dung. Jeremiah sunk in the mire. And Ebedmelech the Ethiopian went to the king: these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, and he is like to die for hunger. The Lord made a way for him, because Jeremiah was set: I am not holding back my tongue anymore, the fire is shut up in my bones; I have to bring the correction and warn the king despite my life. When you step before a king with unpleasant words, as a messenger you might forfeit your life on the spot.

Captain: people might think the Bobby Seale video was just the sixties; we are reading that Jeremiah was in a dungeon, a hole, where the dung came up and he could not avoid it. The same thing, scripturally; it is not far fetched. The Lord constantly reminds us of the mission: do not get comfortable here; you are set on a task. Just as the nations chose their champion, we must constantly declare our champion, Christ the King, the black Messiah. Stay on the mission.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

points: Abedmelech goes to the king and says these men have done evil in all they have done to Jeremiah, who is likely to die of hunger where he is, for there is no more bread in the city; the king commands him to take thirty men and lift the prophet out before he dies.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Abedmelech takes old cast clouts and rotten rags, lets them down by cords, and tells Jeremiah to put them under his armholes under the cords; they draw him up out of the dungeon, and Jeremiah remains in the court of the prison.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Zedekiah sends for Jeremiah into the third entry of the house of the Most High and asks him to hide nothing; Jeremiah answers that if he declares it the king will surely put him to death, and if he counsels him the king will not hearken.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Jeremiah tells him that if he goes forth to the king of Babylon's princes his soul shall live and the city shall not be burned, but if he will not go forth the city shall be given to the Chaldeans and burned; the king says he is afraid of the Jews already fallen to the Chaldeans, and Jeremiah urges him to obey the voice of the Most High that it may be well with him.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Zedekiah charges Jeremiah to let no man know their words, and to tell the princes only that he presented his supplication not to be returned to Jonathan's house; the princes come and ask, Jeremiah answers as the king commanded, and he abides in the court of the prison until the day Jerusalem is taken.

note.label: Jeremiah 38: The Miry Dungeon and Abedmelech's Rescue

points: Nebuchadnezzar gives charge concerning Jeremiah that he be taken, looked to well, and done no harm, but treated as he himself shall say.

note.label: Jeremiah 39: The Fall of Jerusalem

points: The princes of Babylon send and take Jeremiah out of the court of the prison and commit him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to carry him home, so he dwells among the people.

note.label: Jeremiah 39: The Fall of Jerusalem

points: The word came to Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard let him go from Ramah, where he had been bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah being carried away to Babylon; Jeremiah was let go when Jerusalem was seized.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: Jeremiah went to Gedaliah at Mizpah and dwelt with him among the people left in the land.

note.label: Jeremiah 40: Jeremiah Set Free and Gedaliah Made Governor

points: Jeremiah agreed to pray and promised to declare everything the Most High answered, keeping nothing back.

note.label: Jeremiah 42: The Remnant Seeks Counsel and the Most High Says Stay

points: After ten days the word of the Most High came to Jeremiah, and he called Johanan and all the people to hear the answer.

note.label: Jeremiah 42: The Remnant Seeks Counsel and the Most High Says Stay

points: When Jeremiah finished speaking all the words of the Most High, Azariah the son of Hoshaiah, Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the proud men told him he spoke falsely and called him a lying prophet; pride is destruction according to the scriptures.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: Johanan and all the captains took the whole remnant of Judah, the men, women, children, and the king's daughters that Nebuzaradan had left with Gedaliah, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: The word came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews dwelling in the land of Egypt and in the country of Pathros; the Most High reminded them of all the evil He had brought on Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, now a desolation where no man dwelt, because of the wickedness they committed provoking Him to anger.

note.label: Jeremiah 44: The Judgment on the Jews Who Fled to Egypt

points: All the men who knew their wives had burned incense to other gods, and all the women, a great multitude in Egypt and Pathros, answered Jeremiah defiantly.

note.label: Jeremiah 44: The Judgment on the Jews Who Fled to Egypt

points: This is the word Jeremiah spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah.

note.label: Jeremiah 45: The Word of Comfort to Baruch the Scribe

points: In chapter 46 Nebuchadnezzar wipes out Egypt, and then Jeremiah goes back to before that Pharaoh smote Gaza: Philistine is the ancient name for Palestine, and this Pharaoh goes into Esau as in Romans 9 and Revelation 11.

note.label: Zionism in the Face of Syria & Hezbollah

points: Jeremiah commanded Seraiah, when he went with Zedekiah to Babylon, to read all the evil written against Babylon and then declare that the Most High has spoken to cut off this place forever.

note.label: Jeremiah 51: The Full Recompense of Babylon

points: After reading the book, Seraiah was to bind a stone to it and cast it into the midst of the Euphrates, saying, thus shall Babylon sink and not rise from the evil the Most High brings upon her. Thus far are the words of Jeremiah. Rejoice in the destruction of our enemies, which is the salvation of the righteous.

note.label: Jeremiah 51: The Full Recompense of Babylon

points: I Daniel understood by books: what books? The scriptures, the prophecies in the holy Bible. He matched the current events of his time period with the prophecies written in the holy Bible, and he said, wow, I'm in the time that Jeremiah spoke of in Jeremiah chapter 29; this is that time period right now. But if you're not watching and praying, how can you line up what's going on today with the scriptures and know how to move, know how to move in wisdom?

note.label: Perilous Times: Judges and Soldiers

cases.name: Jeremiah
cases.charge: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; be not afraid of their faces: speaking all that was commanded, though the word was a burning fire shut up in his bones and his own familiars watched for his halting
cases.preview: Jeremiah, of the priests in Anathoth, was known and ordained a prophet to the nations before he was formed in the belly, and he prophesied from the days of Josiah to the carrying away of Jerusalem…
